judgments.criterion_verbatim: is the chosen shape honest about its latency and its failure modes -- would an analyst who typed a ticker while the terminal was signed out see a MARKED failure with a reason, or a page that looks like it is still fetching an hour later?
judgments.invocation: org/missions/D5/AMGT/AMGT_RESAPP/deliverables/0.9.0_WK_AMGT_RESAPP~2/SEAM_DESIGN.md sections 5 and 6, read against integrations/bloomberg/research/pull_consumer.py's process_one() and integrations/bloomberg/READ_HERE.md's sign-out rule; no single command decides it
judgments.expect: a reading, recorded with no verdict
judgments.output_evidence: SEAM_DESIGN.md section 5 states, and pull_consumer.py's process_one() implements: bloomberg_health() is called BEFORE every pull; on ok:False, packs/<security_key>/status.json is written {state: FAILED, reason: 'terminal signed out (bloomberg_health ok=False): <health error>'} and the SQS message is deleted -- no automatic retry, no sign-in attempt by this worker or this consumer. So an analyst who submits a ticker while the terminal is signed out would, once a consumer next drains the queue, see status.json move REQUESTED -> FAILED with a human-readable reason naming the health error -- a MARKED failure, not a page that looks like it is still fetching. The one honesty gap this design does NOT close: if NO consumer is running at all (the poller is a person-started/stopped process, or a daily-vehicle-invoked one-shot, per section 2 -- never a persistent service), a request sits at REQUESTED indefinitely with no FAILED/timeout state ever written, and status.json alone cannot distinguish 'about to be picked up' from 'no consumer will ever run.' SEAM_DESIGN.md section 6 states the measured latency (7.6s / 7.7s end to end for a cold request with the consumer launched in the same second) and is explicit that this number assumes a consumer is running; it does not assume an unbounded wait is honest UI behavior, but it also does not build a queue-age alarm (G-20 forbids one) or a status TIMEOUT state for an unattended queue -- left as a named gap for whichever cell next operationalizes the poller's own schedule.

judgments.criterion_verbatim: is the official-vs-impostor test stated in social_accounts.json's schema one that would actually separate a fan account from the company's own, and is the publisher seed's stated rule one an owner could apply without re-deriving it?
judgments.invocation: READ org/missions/D5/AMGT/AMGT_RESAPP/deliverables/0.9.0_WK_AMGT_RESAPP~5/lists/social_accounts.json's `official_vs_impostor_test` field and .../lists/publishers.json's `seed_rule` field, at commit 799ab162d11539f6fe2d489be16f1b1a830e4c48
judgments.output_evidence: OFFICIAL-VS-IMPOSTOR TEST: stated as an OR of three checks -- (1) the company's own measured web presence links to the account by exact URL, (2) the platform's own verification mark is present, (3) the account's bio names the company's registered domain via the display_link-vs-link discipline. It clears the bar PART V asks for in the trivial case (a same-name fan/parody account with NO cross-link, NO verification mark and a bio naming nothing) -- that account satisfies none of the three ORs and is correctly excluded, which a bare name-match rule would not do. DECLARED WEAKEST LINK, read honestly: the composition is an OR across three checks of very different strength, and check (3) alone is CHEAPLY GAMEABLE -- an impostor account can copy the same 'official account of <domain>' bio text a real one would carry, and the test as written admits it on that basis alone, with no requirement that (3) co-occur with (1) or (2). Check (2) is also weaker than it reads today: on at least one major platform, a paid verification mark has been decoupled from identity verification since 2023, so 'the platform's own verification mark is present' is not the strong signal it would have been earlier -- the test does not name this caveat. Check (1) is the strong test (a link FROM a channel already trusted TO the account) but is currently UNUSABLE for all 89 names, because every ir_domain in AMGT-s-12's universe.json is itself UNRESOLVED at this cut (G-24) -- there is no 'company's own measured web presence' yet to link from. So, as stated, the schema is discriminating in principle against the CHEAP case (name alone) but not against a MODERATELY DETERMINED impostor who copies bio text, and its one strong check has nothing to run against yet. A tighter version would require (3) to co-occur with (1) or (2) rather than standing alone, and would flag (2) as weakened by the platform-verification change -- neither of which this schema states. PUBLISHER SEED RULE: an owner applying it needs only to find, in a landed battery finding, a domain named either as an Active estate Lambda's fetch target or as a `display_link` a proven IR-scan measurement resolved to -- both are checkable by reading the cited document section, without re-deriving the underlying research (the rule gives the exact two citations already, eb9cedded6 s.1 and s.3). The rule is honestly SELF-LIMITING rather than incomplete: the brief's own s.4 states the SERP scan 'not run at scale' over the other 88 names, so applying this rule today admits close to nothing beyond the two seeded domains until that scan runs -- a coverage limit the rule discloses (via its own citations) rather than a defect in its clarity. It also correctly excludes marketscreener.com by name, the one case this project has already measured as a trap, which shows the rule is not merely permissive.

judgments.output_evidence: READ lib/research/social/measure.py at commit 0800e9e47919d7e938b9d76dd3af9c02ee72a072. (1) COULD THE NEXT WORKER RUN measure.py WITH THE WORD RECORD AND GET ALL FIVE OBSERVABLES IN ONE CALL, OR RE-PLAN? Partially -- the DATA half is complete and would not need re-planning: DATASET_IDS, FIRST_RUN_DATASET_ID, FIRST_RUN_COMPANY, QUERY_ATTEMPTS (with STOP_RULE), OBSERVABLES, COST_CAP_USD/cost_cap_exceeded(), CANNOT_SERVE_SIGNAL and FOURTH_SURFACE_NOTE are all already module-level data compose_request() reads; the next worker's main() already accepts --word-record and clears the G-24 gate (main(), the 'if not args.word_record' branch) without needing to touch that logic. BUT it could NOT get all five observables in one call as this file stands: past the word-record gate, main() calls compose_request() and then only PRINTS the composed request and returns 4 -- it does not send anything, read a response, or compute any of the five OBSERVABLES (cost, field_schema, latency, freshness, cashtag_queryability), because no HTTP client exists in this module (AC4, deliberate). The next order must ADD: an HTTP client call using the composed request dict from compose_request(); a usage/billing read before/after for 'cost'; a wall-clock timer around the call for 'latency'; JSON parsing of the response for 'field_schema' and 'freshness'; and a call into lib.research.rules.item.qualify() per returned record for 'cashtag_queryability'. That is meaningful new code (an HTTP layer + observable extraction), not a one-line plug-in -- so the honest answer is: the PLAN (what to trigger, in what order, under what cap, with what stop rule) needs no re-planning, but the EXECUTION path (the client and the five observable readers) is not yet written and is new work for that order, consistent with AC4's bound and the worker face's own statement that 'the client is added by the order that carries the word'. (2) DOES THE STOP RULE PREVENT A SECOND TRIGGER IF THE FIRST ANSWERS 'CANNOT SERVE THE FEED'? AS DATA, yes: STOP_RULE and CANNOT_SERVE_SIGNAL both state the condition (all reachable QUERY_ATTEMPTS shapes exhausted with zero admitted records, or the next attempt's estimated cost would exceed COST_CAP_USD) as the point at which the run stops rather than re-triggering a shape already attempted. But AS CODE, this is NOT YET MECHANICALLY ENFORCED: no function in this module currently loops over QUERY_ATTEMPTS, checks a stop condition, or tracks which shapes have already been sent -- compose_request() builds exactly one request per call and main() calls it exactly once. The stop rule is fully SPECIFIED (in STOP_RULE's own string and in MEASUREMENT_PLAN.md s.2) but not yet IMPLEMENTED as a loop with a guard; the next order must write that loop and must not silently drop the guard while doing so. DECLARED WEAKEST LINK: the gap between 'the stop rule is stated as data' and 'the stop rule is enforced by running code' is exactly the kind of thing a later worker could get wrong by re-triggering shape 1 after shape 2 already stopped the run, if it does not carry the STOP_RULE string forward into an actual loop condition. source_rows.one_line: AC4's `echo rc=$?` reports the exit code of `tail`, not of the harness: the invocation pipes node into tail, so a harness that exits 1 on a failed check still prints rc=0, and the criterion's rc clause cannot fail.

evidence: AC4 as written: `cd portal && timeout 110 node src/pages/SecurityAnalysis/__harness__/errorEmpty.harness.cjs 2>&1 | tail -14; echo rc=$?`. In POSIX sh, `$?` after a pipeline is the exit status of the LAST command in it, which is tail; tail exits 0 whenever it can read its input.

Measured both ways on the SAME harness run: the literal invocation prints rc=0, and the harness run unpiped (`node ... > ../.scratch/harness.out 2>&1; echo $?`) also prints 0 -- so the recorded PASS is sound at this cut. The two agree here; the point is that they would not disagree visibly if the harness failed.
The harness DOES set a non-zero code on a wrong-way check (`process.exitCode = 1` beside a 'CHECKS-WRONG-WAY' line), so the signal exists and is simply not reaching the criterion.

source_rows.spec_asserts: AC4 expects 'rc=0 with every prior check still at its met value ... and at least one NEW check naming the unresolved row'.
source_rows.world_is: The rc clause is vacuous; the CHECK lines are what actually carries the verdict. This worker made that half non-vacuous from the harness side rather than by editing the criterion: the harness now prints one `CHECK <name> = <actual> (expected <expected>)` line per check and a final `CHECKS-OK 12 of 12`, all of which survive `tail -14`, so the deciding evidence is IN the graded output instead of behind an exit code the pipeline discards.
source_rows.notes: Both values are recorded in the proof instance: the literal invocation's rc=0 and node's own rc=0 measured unpiped. The generalisable form: any criterion of the shape `<cmd> | tail -n; echo rc=$?` grades the tail, and the fix is PIPESTATUS, a redirect to a file, or -- better here -- making the command's own output carry the verdict.

The defect is older than this cell and is unmoved by it: this cell only changed WHICH measured string is handed to read_point (the identity's bloomberg form instead of the landed block's display form), not what read_point does with it.

source_rows.one_line: The Coverage tab's Star button writes the CANONICAL KEY into a watchlist store keyed by TICKER, so a name starred from that tab can never match a ranked row and lands in the starred residual as an unrankable entry.

evidence: portal/src/pages/SecurityAnalysis/tabs/CoverageTab.tsx:82 @portal 9aef3734, verbatim: onClick={() => setStarredMutation.mutate({ ticker: securityKey, starred: true })} -- the value passed as `ticker` is the page's securityKey.

The starred set is compared against ranked rows by TICKER: LeadPanel.tsx builds `starredTickers` from the watchlist entries' `ticker` field and StarredList.tsx filters `rows.filter((row) => starredTickers.has(row.ticker))`. The server side agrees: read_starred/write_starred carry a `ticker` and delegate to lib/research/watchlist/store.py.
So a star set from the Coverage tab on BABA_US_Equity produces a starred entry that no ranked row (ticker 'BABA US') can ever equal.

source_rows.world_is: Two identifier spaces meet in one mutation argument, on the same page and in the same class as the defect this cell repairs, but in a file this cell's DELIVER list does not name -- so it is filed, not fixed. The remedy is a decision, not an edit: either the watchlist becomes key-keyed (a store change, with a migration for the entries already written) or this button sends the identity block's bloomberg form; picking one silently in this cell would have set the precedent the other cell then has to undo.
source_rows.notes: Worth pairing with whatever cell takes AMGT-rj-5: once ranked rows carry security_key, key-keyed is the cheaper end state and the starred residual stops being a dumping ground for identifiers that never matched.

source_rows.one_line: The contract's database UNIONs two halves that carry DIFFERENT SECTOR VOCABULARIES -- the scanner's 13-value UniverseDataRow.sector and the model block's GICS_SECTOR_NAME -- so rung 1 run on the raw strings returns ZERO same-sector candidates for two of the three landed subjects; the ranker carries a declared GICS-to-scanner map (basis held) with its residue named.

evidence: Measured over the loaded database (candidate_universe.json, vintage 2026-08-06, 2851 rows): the scanner half carries 2849 rows across 13 distinct sector values ['Business Services', 'Consumer Cyclicals', 'Consumer Non-Cyclicals', 'Consumer Services', 'Energy', 'Finance', 'Healthcare', 'Industrials', 'Non-Corporate', 'Non-Energy Materials', 'Technology', 'Telecommunications', 'Utilities']; the model-block half carries 3 rows whose GICS_SECTOR_NAME values are 'Industrials' (BA), 'Consumer Discretionary' (BABA) and 'Information Technology' (SAP).

Exact-string overlap measured: 'Industrials' is in the scanner vocabulary (428 rows); 'Consumer Discretionary' is NOT (0 rows); 'Information Technology' is NOT (0 rows). So a rung-1 test on raw strings gives BABA and SAP an empty candidate set and BA a set from a taxonomy that is not GICS.

The map as built: lib/research/peers/taxonomy.py GICS_TO_SCANNER, 11 GICS sectors -> 12 of the 13 scanner sectors, residue ['Non-Corporate'] (1 row, industryGroup 'Financially Operative Institutions') named in sector_map_denominators(); basis 'held' (an editorial mapping between two published taxonomies), carried in every emitted peer set as sector_map.map_id GICS11_TO_SCANNER13_v1 with the mapped value beside the raw one.

source_rows.spec_asserts: PRD v0.8 group C, ratified: 'the database = the Security Scanner's universe data (UniverseDataRow: ticker, name, mktVal, country, sector, industryGroup, universe weight ...) UNION the harvest universe's model-block header scalars (classification, market cap, country); the rungs, lexicographic, in Andrew's order: same SECTOR ...'.
source_rows.world_is: The UNION is across two classification VOCABULARIES, not one field with two sources. 2849 of 2851 rows speak the scanner's 13-value taxonomy and 3 speak GICS; only the token 'Industrials' appears in both, and the two 'Industrials' do not denote the same set (the scanner carves 'Business Services' out of it). The contract names no map, so the cell either invents one or emits an empty derived set for every model-block subject -- and an empty derived set is exactly what FWD-8 forbids.
source_rows.notes: Disarmed in this order by DECLARING the map rather than hiding it: two GICS sectors map to a PAIR of scanner sectors (Consumer Discretionary -> Consumer Cyclicals + Consumer Services; Communication Services -> Telecommunications + Consumer Services) because the scanner's 'Consumer Services' straddles both, and rung 4 (industryGroup) separates them again; each wide entry carries its reason in SECTOR_MAP_NOTES. taxonomy.residue_over_database() re-measures the map against whatever database is loaded, so a sector value that appears at a later vintage surfaces as UNMAPPED rather than being silently mis-binned (measured now: 0 unmapped sector values). A reader who disagrees with one row of the map can say which row; that is the point of declaring it.

source_rows.one_line: The two halves of the database quote MARKET CAP IN DIFFERENT UNITS -- the scanner's mktVal is USD MILLIONS, the model block's CUR_MKT_CAP is FULL CURRENCY UNITS -- so the 0.2x-5x band on the raw numbers is off by 1e6 and NO candidate clears it for any model-block subject.

evidence: Scanner, sp500/universe_data.json @asOf 2026-08-06: Agilent Technologies mktVal 39918.9 for a ~USD 39.9bn company -- the unit is USD millions.

Model block, org/missions/D5/AMGT/AMGT_RESAPP/deliverables/0.9.0_WK_AMGT_RESAPP~1/model_block_BA_US_Equity.json: CUR_MKT_CAP value 161867780096.00003, and the figure's own basis definition says so verbatim: 'Current market capitalization, full currency units (not millions).' BABA 269839299644.40002, SAP 218452622534.24.

Consequence if not normalised: candidate/subject = 39918.9 / 161867780096 = 2.5e-7, six orders below the 0.2x floor -- every candidate stops at rung 1 and every model-block subject emits basis absent with 'no candidate reaches rung 2'.

source_rows.spec_asserts: The cell: 'the rungs ... then a SIZE BAND (the existing engine's 0.2x-5x market-cap band)' over the UNION database, with the existing engine's MARKET_CAP_MNEMONIC = CUR_MKT_CAP compared against UniverseDataRow.mktVal.
source_rows.world_is: The two fields are the same QUANTITY in different UNITS, and nothing in the contract or the existing engine names the conversion. The band is a RATIO test, which is exactly the shape that survives a unit error silently on one source and fails totally on a mixed one.
source_rows.notes: Disarmed in this order: universe.MODEL_BLOCK_CAP_DIVISOR = 1e6 is applied where a model-block header enters the database and where a model-block subject's own cap is read, the divisor is stated in both module docstrings, and lib/research/peers/tests/test_peers.py::VocabularyAndUnits::test_model_block_cap_is_divided_by_1e6_before_the_band is the red-first arm (a 1e9-unit block must rank against a 1000-million fixture). The emitted subject carries market_cap_raw, market_cap_musd and the block's own unit note, so a consumer can re-derive the conversion rather than trust it.

source_rows.one_line: A model-block subject whose key does not join the scanner's US ticker space STILL HAS a scanner row, under an identifier X-1 cannot resolve -- so SAP SE ranked as its own top peer ('484628', rung 3) until an exact normalised-name arm was added; a cross-listing carrying a DIFFERENT name string is still not caught.

evidence: Measured before the fix: python -m lib.research.peers.engine --security-key SAP_GY_Equity --as-of 2026-09-15 --dry-run printed 'MEMBERS 12 of 94 eligible ... 484628(rung=3) 588950(rung=3) IBM(rung=2) ...' where scanner ticker 484628 is 'SAP SE' (Technology / Software and Consulting / Germany / mktVal 242292.0) -- the subject itself.

The identity plane cannot join them: the scanner's non-US tickers are SEDOL-shaped ('484628' for SAP SE, 'BK6YZP' for Alibaba, '653665' for BYD), and crosswalk.resolve() returns UNRESOLVED for them by design (it never mints a key from a raw identifier). This is the same seam rj-4 measured from the other side: only 3 of 170 ETF holdings joined the crosswalk because that plane's tickers carry no exchange code.

Measured after the fix: 'DATABASE 2851 candidate(s) | universe_vintage 2026-08-06 | minus self 2 (ticker 1, exact-name 1) = 2849 graded' and 484628 is gone from the members; the excluded row is recorded in the object as denominators.self_excluded_by_exact_name = [{'ticker': '484628', 'name': 'SAP SE'}].

The residual, measured: BABA's model block carries NAME 'ALIBABA GROUP HOLDING-SP ADR' while its scanner row is 'Alibaba Group Holding Limited' -- the two do NOT normalise equal, so the arm would not fire. It happens not to matter at this vintage because that scanner row sits in sector 'Consumer Non-Cyclicals', outside BABA's mapped ['Consumer Cyclicals', 'Consumer Services'], so it cannot reach rung 1 at all.

source_rows.spec_asserts: The cell: 'The comparable set of a subject is computed ... by ONE ranker over ONE database' and (the worker face) 'every identity in your objects is resolved through X-1'.
source_rows.world_is: One company can sit in the database TWICE under two identifiers that X-1 cannot join -- the canonical security_key from the model-block half and a SEDOL-shaped scanner ticker from the other -- so the subject is a candidate for itself and, being at distance 0, sorts near the top of its own peer set.
source_rows.notes: DISARM, same turn, by the disarm_owner: the engine now excludes a candidate whose name normalises EXACTLY to the subject's (upper-case alphanumerics, no suffix stripping -- suffix stripping is where a name join stops being an equality and becomes a guess), records both strings in the emitted object, and prints the count on the DATABASE line. The RESIDUAL is left ARMED and stated rather than papered over: a cross-listing whose name string differs is not caught, and closing it needs an identity join the crosswalk does not carry (an ADR-to-local-line join), which is X-1's decision and not this cell's to invent. No live instance exists at this vintage.

U-1's own reason string on an unresolved row: 'the coverage row's bloomberg_ticker status is UNRESOLVED, so no canonical identity is minted for this name (the identifier is NOT guessed from the folder name)'.

Batch measured: 'BATCH as_of=2026-09-15 names N=33 (of 256 universe names; 223 carry no security_key)' / 'DERIVED D=10 ABSENT A=23 D+A=33 N=33 EQUAL' / 'UPLOADED 33 of 33 ... read-back 33 of 33'; s3api list-objects-v2 --prefix peers/v1/ --query length(Contents) = 33.

source_rows.world_is: 'every resolved name' and 'names N from the universe object' are 33 and 256 respectively at this vintage. The batch takes the first reading -- the R-1 key is keyed BY security_key, so a name without one has no coordinate to be written at -- and prints BOTH denominators on its own summary line so the choice is visible rather than inferred. No name with a coordinate is skipped: 10 derived + 23 absent objects = 33 of 33, each absent one carrying its reason.
source_rows.notes: The 23 absent objects are not failures: 22 are non-US keys with no landed model block, whose classification cannot be read without either a Bloomberg call (F2/G-24 forbids it) or a guessed join into the scanner's SEDOL-shaped ticker space; 1 (PBR_US_Equity) is a US key with no scanner row. source_rows.one_line: The size band is graded ACROSS two currencies and two vintages: a model-block subject's cap is in its own trading currency at the block's timestamp (SAP: EUR, 2026-09-10T23:20:18Z) and every candidate is USD at the scanner's asOf 2026-08-06. No FX rate is applied and none is invented.

evidence: model_block_SAP_GY_Equity.json header: CRNCY 'EUR', CUR_MKT_CAP 218452622534.24, figure vintage '2026-09-10T23:20:18Z'. The scanner's six files all carry asOf '2026-08-06' (measured: 6 of 6).

The emitted SAP object carries cap_fx_caveat and the reason string ends with 'CAVEAT: CUR_MKT_CAP is quoted in EUR; the database's mktVal is USD -- NO FX rate is applied and none is invented, so the band is graded across currencies', and the printed SUBJECT line labels the number MEUR, never MUSD.

Magnitude, stated not corrected: at a EUR/USD rate near 1.08 the band's edges move by ~8 percent, which is inside a 0.2x-5x (25x-wide) window -- so the caveat is disclosed rather than remediated, and a rung-3 or rung-4 membership never depends on it.

source_rows.world_is: The gate was fixed to read the PASSAGE and the three measured probes now read REFUSE / PASS / REFUSE -- but on live data it had nothing to check. The model rendered the filing's own sentences without marking them as quotations, so the double-quote extraction found spans on 1 of 85 items and the first drafting document reported 'quoted 0' across 40 of 40 sentences with dropped 0. Remedied inside this cell: the quoted span is now found MECHANICALLY as the longest contiguous run of the sentence's own words that appears verbatim in the EXCERPT (never in the passage it cites), and the gate then checks that run against the CITED passage. export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$(comp-secrets get anthropic-api-key --reveal | grep '^value:' | sed 's/^value:[[:space:]]*//')"  ->  'key len 108 prefix sk-ant- no-space True', and a live 300-token Opus 5 probe returned in 2.2 s.

source_rows.spec_asserts: The cell: 'The key: comp-secrets get anthropic-api-key --reveal (Andrew-direct ~05:4xZ; never a raw secretsmanager read)', and the identity line: 'the Anthropic key reaches your process ONLY as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, exported from comp-secrets get anthropic-api-key --reveal in the same Bash call'.

The working form is comp-secrets get anthropic-api-key --reveal | grep '^value:' | sed 's/^value:[[:space:]]*//' (a pipe-RECEIVER grep, not a gated search). source_rows.world_is: test_the_module_converts_no_identifier_form_into_another reads the module's own source and refuses the literal substrings 'replace("_", " ")' and "replace('_', ' ')" ANYWHERE in it. The guard is text-local by construction and cannot distinguish a security key from a section id, so the first underscore-to-space in the file for ANY purpose fails a test whose message names identifier conversion. The guard was NOT touched: this cell's function was rewritten to the split/join form and the suite is 84 passed, 0 failed.
source_rows.notes: Filed as form, not significance. The guard is doing its job -- AMGT-rj-1's defect was exactly an underscore-to-space inverse applied to a path segment, and a text-local ban is the cheapest thing that cannot be argued around -- and erring toward over-refusal is the right direction for an identifier contract. What costs the next worker is the MESSAGE: it asserts the refused line converts an identifier form, which for line 840 was false, and a worker who believes it will go looking for an identity defect that is not there. A message naming the ban ('this module may not contain an underscore-to-space replace at all; use split/join if you are not converting an identifier') costs one string and no coverage. Not changed here: the test file is AMGT-rj-1's contract surface and re-wording its assertion is not this cell's to do.
